messages:
sara: FYI noticed a repeat pattern after the Dedicated pool rebalance: a small set of tenants cause NIC transmit queues to spike and downstream p99 increases for colocated tenants. looks like noisy egress+nvlink contention.
tony: can you paste the perf dig? link to dashboard would help.
sara: graf: https://graf.company/d/apac/egress-queues?orgId=1&from=now-1h
sara: snippet from host logs: `tx_queue_len` jumping to 9800, `nvlink_retries` increments when these tenants run heavy streaming.
deepa: is this strictly host-level or rack-level? we saw rack-wide NIC saturation before where one uploader killed egress for a few racks.
sara: starts host-level then fans out via top-of-rack when pinned. offenders look like bursty embedding jobs.
ken: thought: instead of hard carving dedicated racks, try soft affinity + per-tenant egress pacing. soft affinity prefers quiet hosts but uses fallback if we've hit pacing threshold. keeps costs down vs cross-az carveouts.
tony: prototype config I hacked in router service:
```
routing:
  affinity_mode: soft
  prefer_hosts: label=quiet
  pacing:
    tenant_window_seconds: 60
    bytes_cap: 150000000  # 150MB/s per tenant window
    on_exceed: fallback_host
  fallback_policy:
    after_ms: 150
    allow_best_effort: true
```
tony: quick 2h sim: p95 improved for tagged tenants by ~60ms, but overall aggregate egress didn't spike. we need 24-72h to see billing delta.
sara: two operational things: 1) add a host tag when nvlink_retries > 5 in 10m so scheduler deprioritizes, 2) expose tenant pacing metrics to billing so we can correlate.
deepa: I worry about quality for embeddings-heavy jobs when we fallback to smaller instances/quantized variants. product needs to OK tradeoffs.
ken: we can have two fallback flavors: bandwidth-fallback (move to host with less NIC load) vs quality-fallback (smaller model). default to bandwidth-fallback.
infra-bot: alert: host-tagging triggered for dedicated/apac-rack12-host7 nvlink_retries=7 in last 10m.
tony: ops checklist: 1) enable host-tagging in canary zone, 2) run soft-affinity+pacing for 48h on 5% of traffic, 3) pipe egress-pacing metrics to billing-run and perf dashboards.
sara: who owns cost estimate? deepa?
deepa: can do a quick calc: assuming 5% traffic shifts, estimate <8% egress cost delta if fallback crosses az; will refine after 48h.
ken: I'll add scheduler change: treat nvlink-tagged hosts as weight=0.2 for 10m. simple roll back if noisy.
tony: command to start canary: `./router_ctl start --policy soft-affinity-pacing --region apac --percent 5 --duration 48h --tag pacing-canary-2026-03-21`
sara: ok starting now. keep thread for post-canary notes. short updates only in this thread pls. :party_parrot:
